title: Hydropower planning, equal weights (W1)

source.citation: Opricovic, S., Tzeng, G.-H. (2008). A comparative analysis of the DEA-CCR model and the VIKOR method. Yugoslav Journal of Operations Research, 18(2), 187-203.
source.location: Section 3 (Eqs. 1-4), Table 1 and Table 7, weight set W1
source.note: The 2004 paper (European Journal of Operational Research 156(2), 445-455, doi:10.1016/S0377-2217(03)00020-1) is paywalled; this open-access paper by the same two authors states the method in full. See docs/methods/vikor.md.

ranking.printedIn: Table 7, W1 (ranked by Q, lower is better)

notes: Hydropower system planning on the Drina river, six alternatives and eight criteria (Table 1): f1 profit, f3 total energy, f4 peak energy and f8 environmental protection are maximised; f2 costs, f5 homes to relocate, f6 reservoir area and f7 villages to displace are minimised.

Strategy weight v = (n + 1) / (2n) = 9/16 for n = 8 criteria, as introduced in this paper (Section 3); the 2004 paper uses v = 0.5. The method must expose v, with 0.5 as the classical default. With v = 0.5 the printed Q values are not reproduced.

Compromise solution: C1 acceptable advantage Q(A(2)) - Q(A(1)) >= DQ = 1/(J - 1) = 0.2, C2 acceptable stability (A(1) also best by S or R). If C1 fails the set is every A(M) with Q(A(M)) - Q(A(1)) < DQ; if only C2 fails it is {A(1), A(2)}.
The paper does not print f* and f-; they are the column best and worst values of Table 1.
W1 gives every criterion weight 1; weights are normalised to sum 1 before use (S never exceeds 1 in Table 7).
